How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy and not cheap either. I joined multiple facebook groups and searched A LOT through those. Luckily I found accomodation for the first month before my arrival and found permanent housing within the first two weeks of my stay. I can def recommend finding more permanent housing after your arrival but be aware that it is going to require some searching and maybee a couple of inspections

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Personally I can highly recommend staying off campus. My host university was situated close to CBD, so it was very hectic around uni. Also, I got to stay in an area that I choose myself, giving me the opportunity to live in an area that I liked and wanted to hang around in.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had differnet guides for the registrations that were easy to follow

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: email support service

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get my initial couses but my host university was very fast in responding and helping me choose the right ones to fullfill the requirements from my home university

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your research. It requires a lot of time to look through the different courses available. My host university provided a list of "pre-approved" courses, but I didn't wanted to be enrolled in any of those - eventhough it might have been an easy option. Decide upon yourself if you are there to study something interesting or if you only want courses that requires "the bare minimum".

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was higher than expected. It might have been a combination of the about of information I had to search myself in terms of working as a landscape architect having to consider social, cultural etc. aspects of country, and the engagement and pressure from peers in terms of wanting to do well and work hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More abstract and more free! But also less structured

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advocacy, Research Cultures and Design Research Studio

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All three of them. Advocacy provided an activistic approach to being a landscape architect. Research Cultures and Design Research Studio are mandatory to be enrolled in at the same time. Research Cultures provides a good foundation for starting my thesis in the coming semester. Design Research Studio had a lot of freedom in terms of what kind of project our group would like to do and what kind of topic we would like to uncover.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Heaps of different ones - I didn't join any of them though

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs that go on trips - makes it easier for you to go out of the inner suburbs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes in the Blue Mountains, travel to Melbourne or Tasmania, enjoy being close to the water

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs like running clubs etc. - be open minded and chat with people. Everyone I have met have been so welcoming!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Practicing landscape architecture in a new country, when you have no information of it political, cultural, social state

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The early mornings. There is very much a "get up and get going"-coffe-morning-exercise culture! And that people are so kind and open

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do your research and decide what you actually want from your exchange stay!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UTS is currently undergoing a lot of changes and the MA Landscape degree is being shut down for now

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning from somewhere and someone else. It is very giving having new perspectives on your own practice.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having enough time to travel australia while my semester was on. Luckily I gave myself 2,5 months of travel after my semester ended!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
